text.text_excerpt: I started staying at the Frenchmen in the mid-80's through mid 1990's and just returned. The only thing that has really changed is the neighborhood. Use to be just The Frenchmen, Checkpoint Charlies & Snug Harbor in this area. Now it's THE place to be for live music & the great location. This room was bigger than any I have stayed in there, with a king bed & balcony overlooking Frenchmen Street. If you are a light sleeper, this could be a problem, with bars open until 2am or later, a fire station right across the street and lots of traffic all day & night. The king bed had nice linens & the matress was very comfy. This room had a tub, which I don't think all of their rooms do. The staff i...

The historic Frenchmen Hotel. I have been wanting to stay here for a while now and finally got the chance. The location is prime being located by the river across from the old US mint. The hotel has wonderful classic New Orleans architecture and is kept in very good shape. The rooms are quite luxurious and the staff is friendly. Parking is located on the property but it is very tight. My Tacoma fit just right but anything much larger would be a challenge. The rooftop has a bar and seating area that goes from 5pm "til". Strong cheap drinks from friendly staff make for a perfect nightcap. Many clubs and restaurants are just a quick cross of the road or a short walk. Many more options open u...

My group of 6 friends spent a long (4 day) weekend at the Frenchmen during Mardi Gras In February. We had a wonderful time, thanks in part to the staff at the hotel. Despite some initial confusion on our part over our reservations (not the hotel's fault, 2 of our group cancelled on the day of our arrival and another 2 wanted to take over their reservations), the transition was completed smoothly and without any anxiety. The staff handled the changes in reservation & credit card info quickly and professionally.
